question: Where do the roof support posts bear: the new slab with thickened footings, existing deck framing, or separate pier footings?
why_it_matters: The bearing path decides whether footings get dug and poured before or with the slab and whether existing deck framing is even present.
unblocks: Excavation/footing tasks, concrete pour scope, framing sequence and post-base hardware procurement

choices: New slab with thickened/turned-down footings at each post
Existing deck framing (as the proposal states)
Separate poured pier footings outside the slab
Unknown — field verify before layout

question: Is the fireplace a framed chase with a Class A metal flue (per the signed drawings), or a site-built masonry chimney?
why_it_matters: The system type sets the footing, chase framing, roof-penetration detail, and the fireplace procurement path.
unblocks: Concrete pour design (fireplace footing thickening), chimney chase framing and roof penetration tasks, fireplace package procurement and lead time

choices: Framed chase + Class A double-wall pipe, brick/stone veneer (drawings p.5)
Manufactured wood-burning firebox in a framed/CMU chase (breakdown basis)
Full site-built masonry with clay flue liner
Not yet decided by customer

question: Does the 2026-12-21 start date stand, given canon bars foundation and framing until mid-February?
why_it_matters: Every phase after demo is concrete or framing, so the plan must know whether the date is real, demo-only, or a placeholder.
unblocks: Plan start anchor, demo timing under the no-demo-without-materials rule, and winter-window placement of slab and roof framing

choices: Move the whole job to a mid-February 2027 start
Date is a placeholder — schedule when selections and permit are in hand
Pull the start earlier to finish slab and framing before mid-December
Start demo/staging Dec 21 and hold concrete and framing until mid-February

question: Do the Aug 20 signed drawings constitute the final fireplace, veneer, hearth, mantel, and screen-door selections?
why_it_matters: Canon forbids scheduling before final selections, and the proposal still records these as open allowances.
unblocks: Scheduling gate, fireplace and veneer procurement orders, mantel clearance check (wood vs non-combustible)

choices: Yes — drawings are the final selections, proceed to order
Fireplace system final; veneer/hearth/mantel samples still open
No — drawings are visualization only, all selections still open

question: Does the existing AC condenser on the rear wall sit inside the excavation/slab footprint and need relocation?
why_it_matters: Relocating a condenser adds an HVAC sub, a mechanical permit, and a dependency ahead of excavation.
unblocks: Utility-relocation task, HVAC sub booking, mechanical permit, excavation start

choices: No — condenser is outside the footprint and stays
Yes — relocate before excavation (change order)
Stays in place but needs protection and clearance during work

question: Will TCR pull a building permit (roof tie-in + solid-fuel fireplace) with inspections for this job?
why_it_matters: A permit adds application lead time before demo and framing/fireplace inspections into the sequence.
unblocks: Permit application task and lead time, framing and fireplace/chimney inspection hold points

choices: Yes — TCR pulls the building permit and schedules inspections (per proposal)
Homeowner pulls the permit; TCR coordinates inspections
AHJ confirmed no permit required for this scope
Undecided — needs written confirmation

question: How many screen doors are contracted, and what unit type?
why_it_matters: A second door adds a framed opening, and a French-style unit has a longer lead time than a stock $125 door.
unblocks: Framed opening layout, door procurement and lead time

choices: One stock screen door on the end wall
Two doors — end wall and back wall
One French-style multi-lite screen door on the back wall
Two doors, one of them French-style

question: Are the 2840DH/3068/5068 openings on the floor plan existing house openings or new units in this job?
why_it_matters: New windows or doors would add a rough-opening, ordering, and flashing task the plan does not carry.
unblocks: Window/door procurement and framing tasks (or confirming none)

choices: Existing house openings on the tie-in wall — no new units
Some are new units (specify which)
All are new units

question: Does the slab extend beyond the screened footprint toward the rear doors/AC pad, as one render shows?
why_it_matters: Extra flatwork changes excavation, gravel, and concrete quantities and the pour duration.
unblocks: Concrete quantity, excavation extent, pour crew sizing

choices: No — slab is the ~12.5 x 23.5 ft footprint only
Yes — slab wraps to the rear doors/AC pad (change order)
Existing walkway stays; no new slab outside the enclosure

question: Which drawing-only enclosure items are in contracted scope: transom/vent band, gutters/downspouts, painted rafters/trim?
why_it_matters: Each adds a task and material order the proposal and breakdown do not carry.
unblocks: Transom framing, gutter install, and exterior paint tasks and their procurement

choices: None — render-only, not in scope
Transom/vent band under the roofline
Gutters and downspouts on the new roof
Painting rafters, posts, and trim white

question: Which knee wall governs: 2 ft white vinyl (proposal) or ~3 ft-4 in lap siding with beadboard interior (drawings)?
why_it_matters: Height and finish change framing quantities, screen bay size, and the siding/beadboard materials to order.
unblocks: Knee-wall framing and finish procurement, screen frame sizing, enclosure labor duration

choices: 2 ft knee wall, white vinyl finish (proposal)
~3 ft-4 in knee wall, lap siding outside, beadboard inside (drawings)
2 ft knee wall but drawing finishes (siding + beadboard)

question: Are there existing roof penetrations (plumbing vents, exhausts, the existing chimney) on the rear slope within the new roof tie-in area?
why_it_matters: Any existing vent that ends up under or against the new roof must be extended and flashed, adding a task and flashing material.
unblocks: checklist item appliance_vent_extension (Extend existing appliance vents through new roof)

choices: None — the tie-in area is clear
Yes — one or more plumbing vent stacks in the tie-in area
Yes — a dryer or range exhaust on the rear slope/wall
Yes — the existing chimney sits at the tie-in and needs flashing work
Unknown until the site visit

question: Is porch electrical (lights, fan, GFCI) confirmed excluded in writing, or being added back before framing closes?
why_it_matters: Adding it later reopens the finished roof/screen work and adds an electrical permit and rough/finish tasks the plan does not carry.
unblocks: checklist item rough_electrical (Rough electrical (circuits, subpanel, boxes))

choices: Confirmed excluded — customer has acknowledged zero electrical in writing
Added back: lights + fan + GFCI on one new circuit
Added back: GFCI receptacles only
Undecided — hold framing close until the customer answers

question: How does the new shed roof tie in: ledger on the house wall below the existing eave, or cut into/over the existing roof slope?
why_it_matters: Cutting into the existing roof adds eave/gutter removal, existing-roof tear-back, and a longer framing and roofing blend.
unblocks: checklist item framing (Framing (floor, walls, roof structure, sheathing))

choices: Cut into the existing roof slope — remove eave/gutter, tie rafters to existing roof framing
Ledger on the house wall directly below the existing eave, no existing-roof tear-back
Sleepers over the existing roof surface at the tie-in
Not yet determined — needs a site visit

question: Is the header beam carrying the rafters over the posts an engineered LVL or dimensional PT lumber?
why_it_matters: An LVL is a separate order with a 1-3 week lead that must land before framing; dimensional stock ships with the framing package.

choices: Dimensional PT (doubled 2x10/2x12) — ships with the framing package
Engineered LVL — separate order, ~10 days
Not sized yet — engineering excluded, decide at framing takeoff

question: Can the ready-mix truck chute reach the rear patio, or does the pour need a pump or buggies?
why_it_matters: A pump or buggy pour changes equipment booking, crew size, and pour-day duration for the slab and fireplace footing.

choices: Truck reaches directly via the side yard — chute pour
Buggies from the driveway — add a laborer and a longer pour day
Line pump required — book pump with the truck
Unknown until access is walked
